| R-02 | Major | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-design/performance-design.md > Illustrative adjustment call (condition line) | The core concurrency design uses the condition `quantity + :delta >= 0`. DynamoDB condition expressions do not allow arithmetic: the grammar only allows operand comparator operand, BETWEEN, IN, functions and boolean combinations (DynamoDB Developer Guide, Expressions.OperatorsAndFunctions, Syntax for filter and condition expressions). Arithmetic is only valid in an update SET clause. The call as designed would be rejected as a validation error. The design also leaves out the upper bound that the contract (Q10) and WF6 step 3 require: an increment that would push quantity above 9007199254740991 must be rejected with 400 and no change. As written, NFR1.1, NFR1.7 and NFR1.12 rest on a mechanism that cannot run and that misses one of the three checks in WF6. | Restate the condition with values computed in the application: for a decrement, `attribute_exists(sku) AND quantity >= :minRequired` where minRequired is the absolute value of delta; for an increment, `attribute_exists(sku) AND quantity <= :maxBefore` where maxBefore is 9007199254740991 minus delta. Keep `SET quantity = quantity + :delta` in the update clause. State how the failed-condition result maps to ItemNotFound 404, InsufficientStock 409, or ValidationError 400 (see the next finding). | New |
| R-03 | Major | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-design/performance-design.md > Pagination bound; scalability-design.md > Bounded reads; traceability.json rows NFR1.4, NFR1.9 | The list design says it reads a bounded page "via DynamoDB Query/Scan with Limit" and returns `total`, `limit` and `offset`, and traceability marks NFR1.4 (no unbounded scans) and NFR1.9 (per-request cost does not grow with item count) as OK. The contract pins offset paging up to offset 10000 plus a `total` count across all pages. DynamoDB has no offset: reaching offset N means reading and discarding N items through Scan pages. `total` needs either a full-table Scan with Select COUNT on every list call, which grows with the table, or a maintained counter, which the design does not mention. A Query needs one partition-key value, and the table is keyed by `sku`, so listing all items is either a Scan or a GSI with one constant partition key, which brings back the hot partition that NFR1.8 rules out. So the OK status for NFR1.4 and NFR1.9 is not backed by a mechanism that can deliver it. | Choose and document a concrete list mechanism that fits the contract: for example, a Scan that skips up to 10000 items, with the cost bound stated honestly (worst case roughly 10100 items read per call), plus a separately maintained item counter for `total` (updated on create and delete) or an explicitly accepted count Scan. Or raise a contract change to cursor paging. Update the NFR1.4 and NFR1.9 traceability targets to match. | New |
| R-04 | Minor | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-design/performance-design.md > Bounded retry row and pseudocode catch block; reliability-design.md > Retry policy | The retry loop catches ConditionalCheckFailed and retries when `isTransientContention(e)` is true. With a single atomic `SET quantity = quantity + :delta`, a failed condition is never a transient conflict: it always means the item is missing, there is not enough stock, or the result would overflow. Concurrent UpdateItem calls on one item are serialized by DynamoDB and do not fail because of each other. `isTransientContention` is not defined, and the design gives no way to tell 404 from 409 from 400 after a condition failure. The things worth retrying are throttling and internal server errors (which the SDK already retries) or a TransactionConflict if transactions are added later. | Retry only on named transient SDK errors (or rely on the SDK retry configuration), never on ConditionalCheckFailed. To classify a condition failure, use `ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure: ALL_OLD` (no old item means 404; otherwise compare the old quantity to tell 409 from 400). | New |
| R-05 | Minor | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-design/scalability-design.md > Blast radius | This section says in-flight requests on a lost instance are "retried by the client / load balancer". The adjustment endpoint is a non-idempotent POST of a relative delta with no idempotency key in the contract. ### Summary

The traceability file is mechanically complete, and the error, observability-field, durability and statelessness designs are sound. But three Major problems stand against the design as written. The security design (the main document under review) still describes no authentication, while the contract requires Cognito JWT. The core atomic-adjustment condition uses arithmetic that DynamoDB rejects, and it leaves out the overflow check. The list design marks bounded per-request cost as met even though offset paging with a total count on DynamoDB grows with table size. Fixing the condition and the paging mechanism, and either updating the auth sections or recording at the gate that they are superseded, would make this ready.
